messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: A couple of feature requests
parts:
Hi Yihui:

I wonder if it's possible to eventually get the following in knitr:

(i) the ability to comment out text/code so that knitr passes LaTeX %
leaders to the .tex file;
(ii) the ability to put captions in graphics without having to produce
a LaTeX figure environment.

The problem with LaTeX's floating figures in a document with a lot of
graphs is that once they start floating, they can get completely out
of whack relative to the text. I really like the way knitr positions
graphics, but it would be even better if one could place captions
below the graphs.

Think of these as wishlist items; since they're more on the LaTeX side
than the R side, I wouldn't be surprised if a 'good' solution would be
difficult to come by.

I really like the new docs on the web site - keep up the great work!

Dennis

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] A couple of feature requests
parts:
1. You are free to comment out code chunks, e.g.

% <<>>=
% # R code
% @

This will not be parsed by knitr. Currently it is not possible to
comment out inline R code with %, e.g.

% here is a piece of inline R code \Sexpr{pi}

will still be parsed and executed. This feature was requested in
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/110 but it looks difficult to
implement.

2. This is almost a LaTeX problem, and I cannot do much about it on
knitr's side. You can force a figure to ignore floating by
\begin{figure}[!h] or \usepackage{float} and \begin{figure}[H]. It is
pretty ticky to deal with LaTeX figure environments, and I think it is
the biggest lie of LaTeX (it frees us of worrying about styles so we
can focus on writing...).

A set of commands that I often use is:

\renewcommand{\textfraction}{0.05}
\renewcommand{\topfraction}{0.8}
\renewcommand{\bottomfraction}{0.8}
\renewcommand{\floatpagefraction}{0.75}

This can alleviate the problem a little bit. It tells LaTeX to give
more freedom to figures; it is often annoying that figures float to
the next page just because we make them slightly larger.

Besides that, make the plots as small as possible (especially the height).

Anyway, it is also possible to ask knitr to write something below the
figures (not using the figure environment) through chunk hooks, but
the main problem is you lose the figure numbers.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] A couple of feature requests
parts:
I didn't expect this would be easy, but I thought I'd ask :) I've used
those LaTeX figure tricks, but when you have a lot of graphs with
little text between them, it doesn't take long before the figures and
the text become disconnected. I much prefer knitr's way of handling
them. I also use the \renewcommand{}'s you listed in my preamble on a
regular basis.

Thanks for the useful reply,
Dennis

Hi Dennis,

I'd agree that controlling the position floats is a purely latex issue.  Have you considered the "float" package with the "H" option? 

Take a look at these and see if it helps address your question:
http://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/8625/force-figure-placement-in-text
http://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/35125/how-to-use-the-placement-options-t-h-with-figures

-Carl
